english: where $p$ and $q$ are positive integers with $\gcd(p,q)=1$. Then the value of $p+q$ is ______.
hindi: है, जहाँ $p$ तथा $q$ धनात्मक पूर्णांक हैं तथा $\gcd(p,q)=1$ है। तब $p+q$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Let $I$ be the integral. Queen's rule on $\left[\frac{\pi}{8},\frac{3\pi}{8}\right]$ uses $x\to\frac{\pi}{8}+\frac{3\pi}{8}-x=\frac{\pi}{2}-x$.

Under this map $\sin x\leftrightarrow\cos x$, so $\sin^{4}x\cos^{4}x$ is unchanged and $\tan x\to\cot x$. Since $\dfrac{1}{1+\cot^{5}x}=\dfrac{\tan^{5}x}{\tan^{5}x+1}$, the two factors $\dfrac{1}{1+\tan^{5}x}$ and $\dfrac{\tan^{5}x}{1+\tan^{5}x}$ add to $1$.
$\csc^{4}u=(1+\cot^{2}u)\csc^{2}u$; with $v=\cot u$, $dv=-\csc^{2}u\,du$, an antiderivative is $-\cot u-\dfrac{\cot^{3}u}{3}$ (continuous on $(0,\pi)$).
At $u=\frac{3\pi}{4}$, $\cot u=-1$: value $1+\frac13=\frac43$. At $u=\frac{\pi}{4}$, $\cot u=1$: value $-\frac43$. Difference $\frac83$.
originality_note: New: the complementary tan^5 factor sits on a non-constant symmetric weight 1/(sin^4 x cos^4 x) over [pi/8, 3pi/8], so after the queen pairing a genuine trigonometric integration remains (way 5). Closest known: int_0^{pi/2} dx/(1+tan^n x) = pi/4 and int dx/(sin 2x (tan^5 x + cot^5 x)) (allen.in). Different because: the weight makes the answer depend on csc^4 integration and the limits are the queen-symmetric pair pi/8, 3pi/8.
blueprint_concepts: Queen's rule: int(a to b) f(x) dx = int(a to b) f(a + b - x) dx
